title: Error Handling in Go
intro: Go error handling is explicit by design — there is no try/catch, no exceptions, and errors are values that flow through the program like any other return value. This module introduces the error interface (one method: Error() string), creating errors with errors.New and fmt.Errorf, the ubiquitous (value, error) return pattern and the if err != nil idiom, wrapping errors with the %w verb in fmt.Errorf (Go 1.13+), creating custom error types by implementing the error interface, and the critical distinction between panic (for programmer errors and truly unrecoverable states) and the error return value (for expected error conditions like 'file not found' or 'user not found'). The comparison question is always 'why doesn't Go have exceptions?' and this module gives the answer Go's designers intended: explicit error handling makes error paths visible, forces callers to handle them, and makes code easier to reason about.
